verbose.label: Show all tool activity
verbose.description: On adds every tool call and its result to the chat, plus the model chip. Off shows only what always appears: replies, delivered files, code edits and shell runs, questions and approvals, reasoning and task lists.
verbose.channelDescription: On relays every tool call and its result to the chat. Off sends only the agent's replies and the files it delivers.

channels.subtitle: Where Wolffish talks to you.
channels.notificationsDescription: Lets the agent send a push notification to your paired phone with its notify_phone tool — when a run finishes, fails, or needs you. Nothing is ever sent automatically; the agent has to deliberately call the tool, and Off makes that tool refuse.
channels.taskResultsDescription: Off keeps the phone's feed clean: replies, delivered files, code edits and shell runs, questions and approvals, reasoning, and errors. On relays every tool call and its result. Connection logging is always on and is not affected by this.

reflection.title: Reflection
reflection.subtitle: Every night, Wolffish reviews its finished conversations — what worked, what failed — and distills the lessons into a playbook it carries into every future turn.

nightly.label: Nightly reflection
nightly.description: Reviews every conversation that has settled since the last pass — automations included — scoring each one and extracting what worked, what failed, and what you liked. The lessons fold into the playbook carried into every turn. Missed fires (asleep, app closed) run on the next launch.

quiet.label: Review after quiet for
quiet.description: A conversation is only reviewed once it has been idle this long, so unfinished work isn't judged early. Anything still warm simply waits for a later night — nothing is ever skipped — and a conversation you continue after its review gets reviewed again with the new turns included.

deepClean.label: Monthly deep reflection
deepClean.description: Once a month, a deep reflection takes the opposite stance of the nightly pass: it challenges the playbook and knowledge files against recent evidence, merging duplicates and pruning stale, over-general, or contradicted entries — the structural guard against learned bad habits.

reflection.runStarted: Started — the result card updates when it finishes.

how.title: How it works
how.pairBody: The QR or code carries a one-time secret. Each device keeps its own key and pins the other's — no account, no password.
how.e2eBody: Everything is sealed on your devices before it is sent. Only this phone and your desktop hold the keys.
how.relayBody: The relay only lets the two devices find each other and passes sealed bytes along — it can't read them and stores nothing.

relayCard.title: Relay
relayCard.body: Where the two devices meet. The QR sets this for you.
relayCard.confirmCompat: It must be compatible with Wolffish — any deployment of the open-source relay works.

pair.hint: Pair once — your conversations, settings and usage follow you.

relay.subtitle: The encrypted link to your desktop
relay.encryptionHint: These four-character forms also appear on your desktop. Matching values mean both devices agree on the keys in use.
relay.privacyBody: Everything between this phone and your desktop is encrypted on the devices themselves. The relay only forwards sealed bytes — it cannot read, alter or replay them, and it stores nothing: no database, no logs, no accounts, no message history. When both devices disconnect, nothing about the session remains anywhere.
relay.reconnectHint: Rebuild the link if it has gone quiet.
relay.unpairHint: Drops the keys and wipes this phone.
relay.unpairConfirmBody: This phone drops its keys and erases the conversations, settings and usage it synced — everything the app holds, back to a fresh install. Your desktop keeps the originals, so pairing again restores them.
relay.demoUnpairHint: Ends the tour and clears the sample data.
relay.demoUnpairConfirmBody: This clears the demo's sample workspace and returns to the start screen. Demo mode stays one tap away, and entering it again reloads everything.

how.pushBody: Your desktop sends changes the moment they occur — a run from anywhere, a renamed conversation, a setting you edited.
how.wakeBody: Every time this app comes back it asks what it missed while it was closed, including anything deleted.

guide.title: Setting automation times
guide.intro: An automation is a schedule heading plus the prompt underneath it. The heading decides when it runs — use one of these forms:
guide.startup: Runs once every time the app launches.
guide.every: Runs on an interval — minutes (m) or hours (h).
guide.hourly: Runs every hour at that minute.
guide.daily: Runs every day at that time.
guide.dailyTimes: Several times a day: list the times, separated by commas. Every listed time runs.
guide.nightly: Same as Daily — reads better for night times.
guide.weekday: Runs Monday through Friday at that time.
guide.weekly: Runs once a week on that day. Day names are in English.
guide.weeklyDays: Several days a week: list the days, then the time. Add more times after a comma to run each day more than once.
guide.monthly: Runs monthly on that day number. Keep it between 1 and 28 so no month is skipped.
guide.monthlyDays: Several days a month: list the day numbers, then the time. Keep them between 1 and 28.
guide.once: Runs one time at that date, then removes itself.
guide.cron: A full cron expression, for anything the forms above can’t say. Join several with a semicolon to combine them.
guide.localTime: Times are 24-hour, in your computer’s local time zone.
guide.chipsTip: The pills above the schedule field fill in a correct schedule for you: pick how many times, then the period — then just adjust the times.

heartbeat.attachAfterSave: Save the schedule and prompt first — files and folders attach to a saved automation.
